record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: Modular surfaces associated with subgroups of PSL(2, Z) can produce Belyi maps and dessins d’enfants. To what extent do modular subgroups connect modular surfaces with dessins d’enfants?

evidence.quote: Question 30. To what extent do modular subgroups connect modular surfaces to dessins d’enfants?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma \le \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ be a finite-index subgroup acting on the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$, and let $X_\Gamma = \overline{\Gamma\backslash \mathbb{H}}$ denote the associated compactified modular surface (a compact Riemann surface obtained by adjoining the cusps). The natural projection $X_\Gamma \to X_{\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z})} \cong \mathbb{P}^1$ given by the $j$-invariant is a covering ramified only over $\{0, 1728, \infty\}$, and after the normalization $t = j/1728$ becomes a Belyi map $\beta_\Gamma : X_\Gamma \to \mathbb{P}^1$ ramified only over $\{0,1,\infty\}$. By Grothendieck's correspondence, $\beta_\Gamma$ determines a dessin d'enfant $\mathcal{D}_\Gamma = \beta_\Gamma^{-1}([0,1]) \subset X_\Gamma$, a bipartite graph embedded in $X_\Gamma$ whose combinatorial type encodes the permutation representation of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ on the cosets $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z})/\Gamma$.

Characterize, as completely as possible, the correspondence
$$\Gamma \;\longmapsto\; (X_\Gamma, \beta_\Gamma, \mathcal{D}_\Gamma).$$
Specifically: determine which Belyi pairs and which dessins d'enfants arise from finite-index subgroups of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ in this way; describe how invariants of $\Gamma$ (index, genus, number of cusps, elliptic points, congruence/non-congruence character, conjugacy class) are reflected in invariants of the associated dessin (passport, monodromy group, valency lists, cartographic group); and explain how the action of the absolute Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ on dessins interacts with this modular construction.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open-ended research problem about the extent to which modular subgroups connect modular surfaces with dessins d'enfants. While the basic correspondence (via the j-line Belyi map) is classical and well-known, and many partial results exist (especially for congruence subgroups and in the work of He, McKay, and others), a complete characterization remains an active and largely open program. No definitive resolution has been published.
